title: Unified Inference: Product Overview, PRD, Roadmap, Pricing & Release Notes (Apr 2027)
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview
--------
This document consolidates the product overview, primary requirements (PRD), high-level design decisions, roadmap & themes, pricing & packaging guidance, and release notes for the Unified Inference product family. The goal of Unified Inference is to provide a single developer experience and runtime that delivers predictable latency, cost, and reliability across Hosted API, Dedicated, and Private deployment modes.

Audience
--------
- Product managers and engineering leads planning roadmap and resourcing
- Eng, SRE, and runtime teams executing design and implementation
- GTM and pricing teams preparing packaging and launch materials
- Solutions and customer success for field enablement

Key objectives
--------------
1. Deliver a unified API and routing control plane with consistent semantics across deployment modes.
2. Provide deterministic latency and cost controls (SLOs, batching, quantization profiles).
3. Offer flexible pricing tiers and packaging that scale from PLG self-serve to enterprise dedicated/private contracts.
4. Ensure a reliable rollout path with telemetry, canarying, and automatic fallback policies.

Context and scope
------------------
Scope: Core serving runtime, control plane features for routing and rollouts, SDK/API ergonomics, policy controls (SLOs/cost), and pricing/packaging. Out of scope for this release: full on-prem install UI; extended compliance add-ons to be handled as separate workstreams.

Product requirements (PRD)
-------------------------
Problem statement
- Teams building LLM features face unpredictable performance and cost when moving from prototypes to production. They need a single runtime that guarantees predictable latency and cost while supporting multiple deployment footprints.

User stories (highest priority)
1. As an engineer, I can call a single REST/SDK endpoint and have requests routed according to latency/cost policies.
2. As an SRE, I can set per-model SLOs and receive alerts if latency or error budget breaches occur.
3. As a platform owner, I can provision Dedicated capacity and pin model versions for tenants with predictable throughput.
4. As a product lead, I can configure quantization and batching profiles and see their unit-cost impact in the console.

Non-functional requirements
- Latency SLOs: 95th percentile token latency <= 120ms on Hosted API for base LLMs under normal load.
- Throughput: Support sustained 1M tokens/min for a region in Dedicated with linear autoscaling.
- Availability: 99.95% monthly uptime for Dedicated customers (SLA).
- Security: Audit logs for all inference requests and KMS integration for Private deployments.

Acceptance criteria (release 1)
- Unified API parity for text-generation, chat, and embeddings with SDKs for Python and Node.js.
- Auto-routing policy UI and API with rule precedence and fallback model variants.
- Cost telemetry: token-level cost breakdowns in console and exportable CSV.
- Canary and A/B rollout tooling integrated into console and control API.

Design & architecture (high level)
--------------------------------
- Control plane: policy management, routing engine, rollout manager.
- Serving runtime: GPU-optimized engine with KV cache, continuous batching, quantization execution paths.
- Smart router: routes by latency, cost, region, and customer tier; supports policy-based fallbacks.
- Observability: per-route tracing, token-level breakdowns, alerting hooks for SLO breaches.

Core design decisions
1. Single API with model aliasing: users call /v1/infer with model alias; router resolves to versioned artifacts.
2. Batching-first runtime: continuous micro-batching to balance latency and cost; per-customer token shaping to enforce SLOs.
3. Deterministic fallback chains: router maintains ordered fallback list; fallbacks must be compatible by output schema.
4. Telemetry-first approach: every decision in routing and rollout emits structured events to the observability pipeline.

Example API usage
-----------------
- Python snippet:

from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key="$REDWOOD_KEY")
resp = client.infer(model="unified-inference-1.2", input="Summarize the following...")
print(resp.output)

- Example routing policy (YAML):

policies:
  - name: low-latency
    match: {region: us-east-1, priority: high}
    actions:
      - route_to: unified-inference-1.2
      - fallback: unified-inference-1.1
      - enforce_slo: p95_latency_ms <= 120

Roadmap & themes (next 6 quarters)
----------------------------------
Themes by quarter:
- Q2 2027: GA of Unified Inference Core (API parity, routing, basic telemetry).
- Q3 2027: Dedicated autoscaling & reservation contracts; improved SLO console.
- Q4 2027: Private deployment packaging (VPC onboarding), KMS/HSM integrations.
- Q1 2028: Advanced Optimize integrations (automatic quantization recommendations), model-level cost-savings suggestions.
- Q2 2028: Large-scale performance tuning (kernel selection, NVLink optimizations).

Roadmap milestones (summary table)
- GA Unified Inference Core — 2027-06-15 — Owner: eng-serving-runtime
- Dedicated reserved capacity beta — 2027-08-01 — Owner: eng-infra
- Private deployment v1 beta — 2027-11-01 — Owner: eng-private-deployments
- Redwood Optimize integration v1 — 2028-02-15 — Owner: eng-platform

Pricing & packaging guidance
---------------------------
Goals for pricing
- Provide a frictionless PLG self-serve tier for dev/test usage.
- Surface cost controls for production customers with committed usage and enterprise packages.

Recommended tiers
1. Free/Tiered Dev — metered per-token with strong rate limits; up to 100k tokens/month free.
2. Production (Usage) — pay-as-you-go per-token pricing with volume discounts.
3. Dedicated — monthly committed capacity with throughput SLAs; base fee + usage overages.
4. Private Enterprise — licensing fee + support; optional deployment engineering and compliance add-ons.

Example pricing matrix (illustrative)
- Dev: $0.00001/token (first 100k free)
- Production: $0.0006/token (0–1M tokens), $0.00045/token (1M–10M), custom enterprise pricing above 10M
- Dedicated: $X,XXX/month base for N vGPU capacity + $0.0002/token over commit

Packaging notes
- Dedicated contracts should include a 12-month commit by default; flexible 3/6 month pilots for large customers.
- Private packages require scope assessment and time & materials for on-prem packaging and network validation.

Release notes (2027-04-01 release — Unified Inference v1.0 beta)
--------------------------------------------------------------
Highlights:
- Unified API: text, chat, embeddings parity across SDKs (Python, Node).
- Routing engine: initial policy language, fallback chains, and canary rollout primitives.
- Observability: per-route latency and token-cost export; SLO alerting hooks.
- Console: routing policy editor, cost breakdown dashboard (beta).

Known limitations:
- Private on-prem installer is not yet GA; limited to managed Private previews.
- Advanced quantization profiles (INT4 auto-selection) are experimental and require manual approval.
- SDK: Go and Java SDKs not yet available; prioritized for Q3 2027.

Bug fixes & improvements
- Fixed intermittent KV cache staleness causing minor tail-latency spikes under heavy mixed workloads.
- Optimized serialization path for streaming responses to reduce CPU overhead by ~12%.

Rollout plan
------------
1. Internal dogfood (2 weeks): product, solutions, and infra teams.
2. Beta cohort (4–8 weeks): invite top 10 existing customers; collect telemetry and regressions.
3. Open beta (6 weeks): PLG signups on Hosted API; limited Dedicated pilots.
4. GA (target Q2 2027): gated on SLO stability and key telemetry thresholds.

Success metrics & KPIs
---------------------
- Time-to-first-successful-inference for new accounts <= 15 minutes.
- p95 latency (Hosted) <= 120ms for base models under normal load.
- Reduction in per-token cost for customers using recommended batching/quantization >= 20%.
- Beta NPS >= 40

SLO & alerting thresholds
- SLO: 99.9% success rate for inference requests within latency SLO per region.
- Alert: >1% error rate sustained for 10 minutes triggers Sev2.

Appendix: rollout checklist (condensed)
--------------------------------------
1. Confirm feature flags and per-tenant defaults.
2. Validate telemetry pipeline and dashboards.
3. Run load tests at 1.5x expected peak.
4. Execute DB schema migration in maintenance window.
5. Announce beta to pilot customers and collect feedback within 2 weeks.

For questions or to request access to the beta, contact the product lead or open an internal ticket in #product-unified-inference.
